result.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
result.summary: The emergence of inverse-designed, pixelated passives for microwave and millimeter-wave applications has been a major development in the field of RFIC design. These devices, which appear to be QR-code-like in structure, exist in a generalizable, high-dimensional design space that includes conventional passive topologies. However, these structures are naturally unintuitive for designers, and failures or deviations in performance are difficult to debug. In this work, we ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict, and edit the responses and layout structure of pixelated passives. The agent, run with all tools disabled, is first asked to read layouts on 18x18 and 27x27 tile grids and, in a single reply, predict the input impedance and loss of the structure from 20-100 GHz. On eight GA-synthesized layouts and five random fills, the predicted Smith-chart locus follows full-wave simulation results closely, with a systematic shift that places features about 16% lower in frequency than EM. On multipath loop structures it identifies notches successfully but shows a smaller frequency bias, about half that of an ideal transmission-line model that ignores bends. The agent is then asked to debug seven designs that fail their specification, and given a budget of five EM simulations and at most twelve changed tiles, it is able to improve all seven and bring five designs within specification. These experiments suggest language models can serve as an interpretability and debugging tool for traditionally non-intuitive inverse-designed passives.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察前沿语言模型在禁用工具条件下能否读取18×18与27×27像素化RFIC无源器件布局，预测20–100 GHz的输入阻抗与损耗，并在五次EM仿真预算内通过改动最多十二块瓦片来调试七个不达标设计。
AI.relevance_reason: 属RFIC设计应用，与VLM推理主线距离较远；但其在有限仿真预算下反复获取证据、筛选布局并决定停止的设定，可能为LVR中几何信息保留与证据获取成本提供类比线索，可供核查。
